content:
maya: Hey, noticed a spike of 429s for customer @acme on their Dedicated pool this morning. They report timeouts and 'rate_limited' errors even though they haven't hit their committed throughput.

maya: Logs show a lot of KV cache eviction churn around the same time. Suspect hot-key / long-context causing backpressure.

julian: Thanks — can you paste the request IDs and a short repro? Also which pool (region, instance-type)?

maya: region: us-west-2, pool: ded-64-gpu-q3. Request IDs: r-8f7a, r-8f7b, r-8f7c. Customer says they run long-context transcripts (30k tokens) with many distinct prefixes.

henry: Quick note: autoscaler didn't trigger extra nodes at that time; capacity stayed at 4 nodes. ops-bot shows no scaling events between 07:12-07:30.

ops-bot: [autoscaler] no-scale-detected: CPU/GPUMem thresholds < scale_up in window 07:10-07:35.

samir: I pulled serving logs:
```
[2026-03-22T07:14:02Z] session r-8f7a: token_gen latency 420ms -> queue wait 310ms
[2026-03-22T07:14:03Z] kv_cache: used=95% max=100% evicted=24MB reason=hot_key_spill
[2026-03-22T07:14:05Z] throttle: 429 generated for session r-8f7a
[2026-03-22T07:14:06Z] kv_fragmentation: free_chunks=12 largest=512KB
```

samir: So cache nearly full and eviction rate high. fragmentation suggests many small allocations (long-context + many prefixes).

julian: Could be hot-key pattern where a few conversation prefixes keep being reused but their KV entries are large. When cache thrashes, runtime starts rejecting requests to protect latency SLOs -> 429.

maya: Customer provided a minimal repro curl that hits the issue:
```
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.com/v1/dedicated/generate \
 -H 'Authorization: Bearer REDACTED' \
 -d '{"model":"rw-large-32k","input":"<long transcript prefix>...","max_tokens":2048}'
```
They send many slightly-different prefixes in parallel.

henry: Two quick mitigations we can suggest immediately: 1) enable prefix caching (config flag) so identical prefixes are reused; 2) bump pool replica count or max_kv_size for this customer as a short-term fix.

julian: Also recommend setting QoS for this customer to prefer latency vs throughput so they don't trigger aggressive backpressure. Add a fallback model with lower KV footprint (e.g., rw-medium-16k) for bursty requests.

maya: I tried increasing max_kv_size to 1.5x in a canary for this customer and evictions dropped in the logs. No more 429s in the next 10 minutes.

ops-bot: [config-change] maya applied patch: pool=ded-64-gpu-q3 max_kv_size=1.5x for customer acme (canary).

samir: Repro steps I used for local sim (if someone wants to run it):
1) spin up a small ded-pool with 4 nodes and default kv limits
2) run 200 parallel requests with 20-30k token context, each with small unique suffixes
3) watch runtime logs for evict events and 429s

julian: For longer-term fix: we should add an autoscale rule to consider kv_eviction_rate as a metric. If eviction_rate > threshold for 30s, scale up or trigger emergency spill to disk/cache tier.

henry: Agreed. Also add better kv compaction to reduce fragmentation (coalesce small chunks). Engineering ticket?

julian: I'll open infra-1962: "Dedicated KV: eviction-driven autoscaling + compaction" with reproducer, logs, and the canary config we used. Assign to eng-runtime.

maya: Customer is happy for now after the canary change, but asked for postmortem and a plan to avoid recurrence.

samir: I'll attach the exact log snippets and the curl load generator to the ticket.

henry: +1. Also flag for support billing: they were near quota, but throttles were internal protection not billing enforcement. Need clear customer comms.

maya: Drafting comms now: explain root cause (KV pressure from long-context hot-keys), short-term mitigation we applied (bumped max_kv_size canary + prefix cache), and long-term plan (eviction-driven autoscale + KV compaction + QoS routing).

julian: Nice. Add recommended customer config: enable prefix_cache=true, set fallback_model=rw-medium-16k, increase reserved_replicas by 1.

maya: I'll send the message and close the support ticket when infra-1962 is filed. Thanks everyone :thumbsup:

ops-bot: [ticket-created] infra-1962 by julian - Assigned to eng-runtime - priority P2

julian: Keeping this thread for notes; move to eng-runtime for tracking.
